disease_label_per_paper: Systemic salicylate toxicity from chronic topical use of an over-the-counter 2% salicylic acid cream in a 6-month-old infant with suspected ichthyosis
presentation_summary: 6-month-old unvaccinated girl (4.56 kg) without routine pediatric care presented with poor feeding, emesis, and progressive lethargy over several days, with increased irritability and vomiting on the day of presentation.

Persistent pruritic dry rash since 3 months of age treated at home with an over-the-counter 2% salicylic acid product multiple times daily for several months (last application the morning of presentation), plus calendula oil/vitamin E and herbal teething drops (clove and spearmint oils).
ED: afebrile, ill-appearing, listless, clinically dehydrated (dry mucous membranes, sunken eyes), tachypneic, HR 204, BP 69/25 mmHg; diffuse erythematous dry scaly rash without vesicles or pustules.
Initial VBG pH 6.98, HCO3 5.7 mmol/L, pCO2 22 mmHg; lactate 12.15 mmol/L; potassium 6.2 mmol/L with peaked T waves; albumin 2.6 g/dL; PT 86.8 s, INR >9.36; head CT unremarkable.

record_only_findings.finding: Tachypnea without a reported respiratory rate
record_only_findings.note: Not structured as tachypnea_presence because the runtime loader expands tachypnea_presence=1 into respiratory_rate=1.0 breaths/min, which would inject an impossible numeric value; respiratory compensation is represented by venous pCO2 22 mmHg.

later_course_record.finding: Early PICU course: urine output 23 mL over 24 h (~0.2 mL/kg/h); peak AST 95 U/L, ALT 134 U/L; fibrinogen later 80 mg/dL; platelet nadir 46 x10^3/uL; hypoalbuminemia with third-spacing; no bleeding
later_course_record.source_text_value: Early in her PICU course, urine output decreased to 23 mL over 24 hours ... peak AST 95 U/L ... ALT 134 U/L ... fibrinogen later decreasing to 80 mg/dL ... platelet count decreasing to a nadir of 46 ×10³/µL

later_course_record.finding: Within 24 h mental status improved; pH normalized with bicarbonate; salicylate 31 -> 18 -> 7.4 mg/dL over 48 h
later_course_record.source_text_value: Within 24 hours of admission, her mental status had improved ... her salicylate concentration declined from 31 mg/dL on admission to 18 mg/dL within 24 hours and 7.4 mg/dL within 48 hours.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Serum salicylate concentration 31 mg/dL on admission (reference <6)
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Toxicologic testing was notable for an elevated serum salicylate concentration of 31 mg/dL.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Urine drug screen negative; viral testing negative; DAT normal (no hemolysis); echocardiogram and abdominal/pelvic duplex unremarkable
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Head computed tomography was unremarkable, viral testing was negative, and urine drug screening was negative. ... Workup was negative for hemolysis, with a normal direct antiglobulin test

confirmatory_findings.finding: Dermatology: ichthyosis vs severe atopic dermatitis; genetic testing nondiagnostic (SLC27A4 VUS)
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Dermatology evaluation raised concern for ichthyosis versus severe atopic dermatitis, and genetic testing was nondiagnostic except for a variant of uncertain significance in SLC27A4.

actual_treatment: intravenous sodium bicarbonate with urinary alkalinization
topical corticosteroids, bland emollients, wet wraps; discontinuation of salicylic acid products

outcome.source_text_value: The patient improved without dialysis and was discharged with dermatologic care instructions and close subspecialty follow-up.

quality_warnings: Serum salicylate concentration is the diagnosis-establishing test and is non-ranking; the topical salicylic acid exposure history (as written in the case presentation) is rankable exposure evidence.
PT/INR/albumin are taken as presentation values per the Table 1 caption; the narrative places the coagulopathy within the PICU course, so their timing is somewhat uncertain.
INR is censored (>9.36) and recorded at the lower bound.
No temperature value, respiratory rate, sodium, chloride, anion gap, or glucose reported; tachypnea kept record-only because of a loader alias (tachypnea_presence -> respiratory_rate=1.0).
Loader alias: venous_pco2 is also expanded to arterial_pco2 (same value); fever_presence=0 is expanded to infection_trigger_activity=0.
